rights.notes: Only independently written factual metadata and outbound links are redistributed; no source prose or creative asset is copied.

review.notes: Claims were checked against the linked primary or regulatory source. Evidence and causality are stated conservatively; independent human review is encouraged.

objective: Acquire teams through self-service use and expand adoption inside organizations.
businessContext: Enterprise collaboration software typically depended heavily on top-down selling and lengthy implementation.
strategy: Let users experience a free product, advocate internally and expand usage, supported by sales and customer success for larger deployments.
outcomes: Slack reported more than 10 million daily active users and over 88,000 paid customers as of January 2019, rising above 95,000 paid customers by April 2019.
whatWorked: The product itself created evidence and advocacy before enterprise purchase.
Customer success supported expansion after initial adoption.
whatFailed: The filing does not isolate product-led mechanics from sales, category growth or brand effects.
transferConditions: Users can adopt safely at small scale and value increases with team participation.
nonTransferConditions: Do not apply frictionless self-service where security, integration or procurement requires up-front enterprise control.

sources.title: Slack Technologies registration statement
sources.methodology: Company filing describes the go-to-market model and audited business-scale disclosures; it does not isolate marketing causality.
